title: Canonical affine polynomial coordinates of the singular fibre
statement: Let k be a field, f:Y -> Spec k any morphism, L any module sheaf, and s_i any finite family of global sections indexed by I in the scheme universe. Use the universal family and reduced singular scheme [def-zl-bertini-universal-family]. For any open U of Y and z in U, let T=(bertiniSingularToSource f L s restricted to U)_z be the actual scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and K=kappa_U(z). Its coefficient projection to Spec k[x_i] and its structure map to Spec K agree over Spec k. The polynomial base-change square therefore defines a unique morphism h:T -> Spec K[x_i] with these two projections. This h is a closed immersion. Its actual coordinate ring map rho:K[x_i] -> Gamma(T,O_T), obtained by composing GammaSpecIso.inv with h.appTop, is surjective, and T.toSpecGamma followed by Spec rho is h. No smoothness, invertibility, generation, immersion or rank hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Tag 0FD6, lemma-bertini, universal-family diagram; Schemes lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes and Morphisms lemma-closed-immersion-affine

proof.text: The Mathlib polynomial algebra pushout instance, CommRingCat.isPushout_of_isPushout, and isPullback_SpecMap_of_isPushout give the polynomial base-change square. The fibre projection identity and the restriction square show that its two actual projections agree over k. Define h by the unique pullback lift.

Paste the fibre square with the restriction square. Cancel the ambient product square from the polynomial base-change square to obtain the ambient fibre square. The projection identities make the square from T to the original singular scheme a pullback of the composite of its two closed inclusions. Stability under base change therefore proves IsClosedImmersion h.

Apply IsClosedImmersion.isAffine_surjective_of_isAffine to h. Composing h.appTop with GammaSpecIso.inv gives the stated surjective rho. Naturality of toSpecGamma and the Gamma-Spec triangle identity give T.toSpecGamma >> Spec rho = h.
